research_mode: official OSR and ONS sources only; police recorded crime quality oversight, CSEW and police-recorded divergence, current March 2026 measurement boundaries and designation controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: NDQIS force availability
verified_claims: NDQIS is available to 42 forces
usage information is reported in relevant datasets
availability does not mean identical use by every force
limitations: the unavailable force and usage differences must remain explicit
tool availability is not proof of complete flag coverage

sources.name: September 2025 police-recorded volume
verified_claims: police recorded 6.7 million crimes in year ending September 2025
the level was similar to the previous year
the bulletin compared this with 4.2 million in year ending March 2015
limitations: the series includes offence groups with recording discontinuities
the national total is not a local rate

sources.name: Recorded-crime growth interpretation
verified_claims: ONS said increases since March 2015 were largely driven by police activity and recording practices
some movement may reflect genuine crime changes
police recorded crime is not generally a reliable indicator of overall crime trends
limitations: the statement concerns overall trends rather than every offence type
recording influence does not mean all growth is artificial

sources.name: Use for lower-volume higher-harm offences
verified_claims: police recorded crime provides insight into lower-volume higher-harm offences
examples include homicide and weapons offences
robbery is another offence type highlighted for police-recorded analysis
limitations: fitness remains dependent on reporting and recording quality
higher harm is not a numeric parcel score

sources.name: CSEW and police-recorded designation split
verified_claims: CSEW estimates are accredited official statistics
police recorded crime data are not accredited official statistics
the two designations must be retained separately
limitations: accreditation does not remove survey uncertainty
non-accreditation does not make all police data unusable

sources.name: Figure-label correction without data change
verified_claims: ONS corrected two figure data-point dates on 10 April 2026
the corrected labels were year ending September 2024 and September 2025
ONS stated that no data values changed
limitations: metadata corrections and data corrections must be distinguished
superseded versions should not be silently mixed

sources.name: Pandemic survey estimate gap
verified_claims: CSEW estimates for year ending March 2021 are unavailable
estimates for year ending March 2022 are also unavailable
the gap resulted from suspension of face-to-face interviewing
limitations: missing survey years are not zero crime
telephone-survey outputs require separate mode metadata

sources.name: Report Fraud system transition
verified_claims: Report Fraud launched on 4 December 2025
the system replaced Action Fraud for national fraud and cybercrime reporting
ONS said subsequent bulletins would no longer refer to Action Fraud
limitations: system transition can create series and processing changes
launch date is not an incident-date boundary

sources.name: December 2025 release designation
verified_claims: the December 2025 crime release was published on 23 April 2026
CSEW content was labelled accredited official statistics
police recorded crime content was labelled official statistics
limitations: designation is component-specific within the release
release date differs from the reference period

sources.name: CSEW open-table dimensions
verified_claims: the release provides personal and household crime open tables
tables include demographic and household breakdowns
incidence and prevalence are published as separate products
limitations: open-table combinations can have different bases and precision
national survey tables do not supply parcel observations
